Date range

Pick a range — up to 30 days at a time — for emails sent, response rate and conversion rate over that period. Response/conversion rate is measured against that range's own new-contact cohort: of everyone first contacted in the range, what share have gone on to reply, or convert, as of right now (so a reply that landed after the range ended still counts for the batch that produced it).

Month on month

Same cohort method as above, one row per calendar month: everyone first contacted that month, and what share of them have gone on to reply or convert as of today.
"Emails sent" counts every outbound touch logged in a contact's follow-up history — initial sends, cascade chases, mailshots and extra one-off touches like a discount blast — across both brands. It excludes reply/outcome records, which aren't sends. A contact's own reply, whether logged as neutral, negative or handed to a rep, counts toward "response rate"; a bounce does not, since nobody read it. "Conversion rate" counts contacts handed to a rep as a genuine enquiry. Figures are current as of the last refresh — see the freshness note above.

🔔 Replied — needs your call

A reply came in that the morning Outlook check couldn't confidently classify as clearly negative — have a quick read and mark it yourself. Tapflo only for now; see the footnote below.

🔄 Interested — chasing next step

Genuine interest, but it isn't a done deal and it isn't a real Salesforce enquiry yet — there's still legwork on your side (an EPCm to loop in, a call to actually get booked, someone to nudge) before it either lands as a real conversion or needs writing off. Not part of the cold cascade — these get chased manually, on your own timeline.

📬 Ready to send

Nothing being chased right now. Head to the Cold Lead Action Desk, open a draft in Outlook and send it, then click "Start Follow-Up Tracking" underneath that contact — it'll show up here the moment you do.

📅 Pending — coming up

Not due yet — just a preview so you can see what's next. Nothing here needs action; it moves up to "Ready to send" on its own due date (dates never land on a weekend or UK bank holiday — they roll to the next working day).

📭 Opted out / bounced / removed / undeliverable

Everyone out of the cascade, kept here as a record with the reason: opted out, replied negatively, removed by hand, or the email never landed. Removals are deliberately not counted as conversions. Not all of these are dead ends. A delivery failure where the receiving server rejected the message on spam or policy grounds means the address itself is almost certainly fine, so those are sorted to the top with an amber flag and are worth a phone call or a resend. A genuine unknown-recipient bounce is a dead address and sits below it in grey. The counts underneath say how many of each you have.
Tapflo leads: a scheduled check runs every morning against Outlook Sent/Inbox and Salesforce — it starts tracking on any email it finds was actually sent, pulls out anyone who's replied (auto-removing clear "not interested" replies as negative, flagging anything less obvious above for you), and permanently retires anyone who's become a real Salesforce enquiry/opportunity so they're never chased again. Sychem leads aren't covered by that check yet — Outlook can't see Sychem's mailbox from this connection, and Sychem has no CRM to check against — so Sychem still relies on you clicking "Start Follow-Up Tracking" and the outcome buttons yourself. Mailshot content flagged ⚠ is a placeholder template — swap in a real, anonymised recent project before sending; company names should never appear in mailshot copy. 18 Aug fix: tried deep-linking "Open in Outlook — Reply-All" straight into a real Outlook Web thread reply, but that reliably failed (ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE) once actually tested against a live mailbox — the New Outlook client intercepts those links into its own webview and the reply viewmodel doesn't render through it. Reverted to the mailto: link, since that's confirmed to reliably open the real desktop Outlook compose window rather than a browser tab — it's a new email rather than a true header-level reply (mailto: has no way to attach to a real sent item), but the body now quotes a Sent/To/Subject block above your original message, the same layout Outlook's own quoted replies use, so it reads the same way once it lands. A real Reply-All is still possible — it just can't be triggered from this page, only from inside Outlook itself (a static webpage has no way to reach in and fire an Outlook command). That's what the "Follow-Up Reply" Outlook Add-in is for, pending your IT admin deploying it: a "🔎 Open Original Email in Outlook" button appears wherever the real message ID is on file, which jumps straight to that email (this part is confirmed working, unlike the reply deep link) — from there, clicking the add-in's own ribbon button gives a genuine native Reply-All with the suggested text pre-filled. 19 Aug update, link behaviour — resolved: a run of guesses chased this the wrong way — it wasn't a Claude dialog, wasn't Windows Default Apps, wasn't Chrome's installed-apps list, and removing target="_blank" didn't fix it either. Along the way a microsoft-edge: prefix was added to force the link into Edge specifically, which did get it into a real browser tab — but the error that showed there next (OwaUserHasNoMailboxAndNoLicenseAssignedException) was the real giveaway: the browser's Outlook Web session was signed into an account with no licensed mailbox attached, nothing to do with the link itself. Aidan confirmed this directly by diffing a working local copy of this portal against the current one — the link code was byte-for-byte identical in both, proving the link was never the problem. Once signed into the correct aidan@tapflopumps.co.uk account in the browser, the plain link opens the real email immediately. The microsoft-edge: prefix has been removed and target="_blank" restored — back to the original, simplest form, which is correct. Standing rule going forward, this portal and any future one: keep "Open Original Email in Outlook" as a plain https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?ItemID=...&viewmodel=ReadMessageItem link (the same URL Microsoft Graph's own webLink field returns for a message) opened with target="_blank" rel="noopener" — no URI-scheme tricks, no dropping target="_blank". If it ever fails again, check which Microsoft account is signed into the browser before touching this code.
